docs.title: BreathTrailer Owner’s Manual
docs.text:
Official Technical & User Documentation

Designed for safe operation, off-grid camping, and everyday usability — this manual provides clear guidance on how to operate all systems installed in your BreathTrailer Essential/Plus/Ultra/Max.

docs.title: Welcome
docs.text:
This manual has been created to help owners confidently use their trailer without the need for constant technical support.

Whether you are camping off-grid or connected to site power, this guide explains how each system works and how to use it safely.

docs.title: What This Manual Covers
docs.text:
• 🔋 Power Systems Battery charging, solar, inverter, and 240V city power

  • 💧 Water Systems Clean water, grey water, hot water system, and kitchen sink

  • ❄️ Appliances Fridge operation, stove and 12V systems

  • 🌤️ Outdoor Equipment Awning, shower tent, and external features

  • 🛠️ Maintenance & Safety Daily operation, troubleshooting, and long-term care

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
If this is your first time using the trailer, start here:

  • 👉 Getting Started Trailer coupling, safety information, and first use

  • 👉 Power Systems How to manage battery, solar, inverter, and camp power

  • 👉 Water Systems Tanks, hot water, and kitchen sink operation

  • 👉 Maintenance & Troubleshooting Daily checks and common issues

Use the navigation menu on the left to access each section.

Warning

Always read the Safety Information section before operating electrical or gas systems. Incorrect use may result in damage, injury, or loss of warranty.

docs.title: Built for Adventure
docs.text:
The BreathTrailer is designed for reliability, simplicity, and off-grid capability.

This manual will be updated as systems evolve — always refer to the latest version when operating your trailer.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Welcome to the official BreathTrailer Owner’s Manual.

This manual has been designed to help you safely and confidently operate all systems installed in your BreathTrailer without the need for technical assistance.

Please read this manual carefully before using the trailer for the first time. Correct operation ensures safety, system reliability, and long-term performance.

docs.title: Purpose of This Manual
docs.text:
This manual provides clear instructions for the operation, use, and basic maintenance of all major systems installed in the trailer.

It is intended for: - Trailer owners - Campers and off-grid users - Anyone responsible for towing, operating, or maintaining the trailer

docs.title: What This Manual Covers
docs.text:
This manual includes detailed information about:

  • Trailer coupling and safe towing procedures
  • Battery charging methods and solar systems
  • 12V and 240V power systems
  • Inverter and City Power operation
  • Hot water and water systems
  • Fridge, lighting, and electrical appliances
  • Awning and shower tent setup
  • Daily operation, maintenance, and troubleshooting

docs.title: How to Use This Manual
docs.text:
For first-time users: 1. Start with the Quick Start Guide on the home page. 2. Review the Safety Information section. 3. Read the Trailer Coupling & Handbrake section before towing.

For regular use: - Refer to individual sections as needed using the navigation menu. - Follow all warnings and notes to avoid damage or unsafe operation.

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• This trailer is designed for camping and off-grid use.
  • Always operate systems within their specified limits.
  • Do not modify any installed systems unless approved by an authorised technician.

Failure to follow the instructions in this manual may result in equipment damage, unsafe operation, or loss of warranty.

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text:
If you require service, support, or technical assistance, refer to the Support & Contact section of this manual.

Thank you for choosing BreathTrailer. We wish you safe travels and enjoyable adventures.

docs.title: Safety Information
docs.text:
This section contains important safety instructions for the safe operation, towing, and use of your BreathTrailer.

⚠️ Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury, equipment damage, or loss of warranty.

docs.title: General Safety Guidelines
docs.text:
• Always read and understand this manual before using the trailer.
  • Only operate the trailer and its systems as described in this manual.
  • Do not modify or alter any installed system unless approved by an authorised technician.
  • Keep this manual accessible at all times.

docs.title: Towing & Road Safety
docs.text:
• Always ensure the trailer coupling is correctly locked onto a 50mm tow ball.
  • Safety chains must be attached and crossed underneath the coupling.
  • Ensure the trailer handbrake is fully released before towing.
  • Verify that the electrical plug is connected and functioning correctly.
  • Never exceed the trailer’s rated towing or load limits.
  • Drive at safe speeds suitable for road and weather conditions.

⚠️ Never tow the trailer with the handbrake engaged.

docs.title: Electrical Safety
docs.text:
• 12V and 240V systems operate differently and must be used correctly.
  • Always check the power selector switch position before using 240V outlets.
  • Do not use damaged cables, plugs, or electrical equipment.
  • Do not overload the inverter.
  • High-power appliances such as kettles, heaters, air fryers, and hair dryers must not be used with the inverter.

⚠️ Improper electrical use may cause system shutdown or damage.

docs.title: Battery Safety
docs.text:
• Batteries must not be exposed to excessive heat, water, or physical damage.
  • Ensure adequate ventilation around battery systems.
  • Do not short-circuit battery terminals.
  • Turn off unused electrical systems to prevent excessive battery discharge.

docs.title: Gas Safety
docs.text:
• Only use approved LPG gas cylinders with the correct Australian-standard connection.
  • Ensure gas connections are secure before use.
  • Never operate gas appliances in enclosed or poorly ventilated spaces.
  • Turn off gas supply when the hot water system is not in use.

⚠️ Gas misuse can result in serious injury or fire.

docs.title: Water System Safety
docs.text:
• Ensure the water pump is switched ON only when water is available in the system.
  • Do not operate the pump dry for extended periods.
  • Drain water systems when required, especially before long-term storage.

docs.title: Awning & Outdoor Equipment Safety
docs.text:
• Do not deploy awnings in strong winds or extreme weather.
  • Ensure the vehicle is stationary with the handbrake applied before setup.
  • Always pack away awnings and tents immediately if weather conditions worsen.

docs.title: Maintenance & Inspection
docs.text:
• Regularly inspect the coupling, safety chains, electrical connections, and gas fittings.
  • Address any damage or faults before using the trailer.
  • Only use authorised parts and service providers.

docs.title: Emergency Situations
docs.text:
• In the event of electrical, gas, or water system failure, switch off the affected system immediately.
  • If a fire risk is suspected, disconnect power and gas supplies if safe to do so.
  • Seek professional assistance before resuming use.

By following these safety guidelines, you help ensure safe operation, system reliability, and long-term performance of your BreathTrailer.

docs.title: Trailer Coupling & Handbrake
docs.text:
This section explains how to safely connect and disconnect your BreathTrailer from the tow vehicle, as well as how to correctly use the trailer handbrake.

Correct coupling is essential for safe towing and legal road use.

docs.title: Coupling System Overview
docs.text:
The BreathTrailer is equipped with a 50mm electric brake trailer coupling with an integrated manual handbrake.

⚠️ Only a 50mm tow ball must be used. Using an incorrect tow ball size is unsafe and illegal.

docs.title: How to Hitch the Trailer
docs.text:
Follow these steps every time you connect the trailer to a vehicle:

  1. Park the tow vehicle on level ground and apply the vehicle handbrake.
  2. Ensure the trailer handbrake is engaged.
  3. Raise the trailer using the jockey wheel.
  4. Align the coupling directly above the 50mm tow ball.
  5. Lower the coupling onto the tow ball until fully seated.
  6. Push the coupling handle down firmly until it locks.
  7. Attach the safety chains to the vehicle, crossed underneath the coupling.
  8. Connect the trailer electrical plug to the vehicle.
  9. Slowly raise the jockey wheel fully and secure it in the travel position.
  10. Release the trailer handbrake only after all steps above are completed.

docs.title: Coupling Lock Check
docs.text:
After hitching, always perform this safety check:

  • Gently raise the jockey wheel.
  • If the rear of the tow vehicle lifts slightly, the coupling is locked correctly.

⚠️ If the coupling does not lock securely, do not tow the trailer.

docs.title: How to Unhitch the Trailer
docs.text:
1. Park the vehicle on level ground and apply the vehicle handbrake.
  2. Apply the trailer handbrake.
  3. Lower the jockey wheel until it supports the trailer weight.
  4. Disconnect the electrical plug.
  5. Remove the safety chains.
  6. Unlock the coupling handle.
  7. Raise the trailer coupling off the tow ball using the jockey wheel.

docs.title: Applying the Handbrake
docs.text: • Pull the handbrake lever fully upward until it locks.

docs.title: Releasing the Handbrake
docs.text:
• Push the handbrake lever fully downward before towing.

⚠️ Never tow the trailer with the handbrake engaged. This will cause brake damage and unsafe driving conditions.

docs.title: Safety Notes
docs.text:
• Always double-check the coupling lock before driving.
  • Inspect the coupling and safety chains regularly for wear or damage.
  • Never exceed the trailer’s rated load or towing capacity.
  • If any component appears damaged or worn, do not tow the trailer until repaired.

Correct coupling and handbrake operation are critical for safe towing and long-term reliability of your BreathTrailer.

docs.title: Battery Charging
docs.text:
This section explains all available battery charging methods installed in the BreathTrailer.

The trailer is designed to keep the battery charged automatically whenever possible, reducing the need for manual intervention.

docs.title: Battery Charging Overview
docs.text:
The BreathTrailer battery can be charged using multiple power sources:

  • Roof-mounted solar panel
  • Camp site (City Power) electricity
  • Optional external solar blanket

Charging is managed automatically by the installed charging systems.

docs.title: Solar Charging (Primary Source)
docs.text:
The primary charging source is the solar panel mounted on top of the trailer.

  • The battery is charged continuously whenever sunlight is available.
  • Solar charging starts and stops automatically.
  • No user setup or configuration is required.

☀️ Solar charging operates only when sufficient sunlight is present.

docs.title: Camp Site Power Charging (City Power)
docs.text:
The battery can also be charged using camp site electricity.

Installed Battery Charger

A 22A / 32A battery charger is installed inside the trailer box.

How to Charge Using Camp Site Power

  1. Connect the supplied 15A power lead to the camp site outlet.
  2. Plug the other end into the trailer box power inlet.
  3. Battery charging will start automatically.

✔️ The battery charger manages charging safely and efficiently.

docs.title: Charging While Towing
docs.text: When the trailer is connected to the tow vehicle, the battery may receive supplementary charging depending on the installed system configuration.

docs.title: Charging Status
docs.text:
• Battery status can be checked on the battery box display.
  • Charging occurs automatically based on available power sources.

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• Multiple charging sources can operate simultaneously (for example, solar and camp site power).
  • Charging systems are designed to protect the battery from overcharging.
  • Do not connect unapproved chargers or power sources.

⚠️ Incorrect charging connections may damage the battery or charging system.

Proper battery charging ensures reliable operation of all 12V and 240V systems installed in your BreathTrailer.

docs.title: 12V Power System
docs.text:
This section explains how the 12V power system operates in the BreathTrailer and which components are supplied directly from the battery.

The 12V system is the primary power system used during off-grid operation.

docs.title: 12V Power Overview
docs.text:
All 12V power in the BreathTrailer is supplied directly from the battery.

The 12V system operates independently from camp site power and remains available as long as the battery has sufficient charge.

docs.title: 12V Powered Components
docs.text:
The following components operate on 12V power:

  • Interior lighting
  • LED light bars
  • Fridge (12V)
  • Water pump
  • Fans
  • USB charging outlets (if equipped)

✔️ These systems are available even when the trailer is not connected to camp site power.

docs.title: Main 12V Power Switch
docs.text: A main 12V power switch is located inside the trailer box.

docs.title: Operation
docs.text:
• Switch ON to supply power to all 12V systems
  • Switch OFF to isolate 12V power when the trailer is not in use

Turning off the main 12V switch helps prevent unnecessary battery discharge.

docs.title: Battery Dependency
docs.text:
Because all 12V systems are powered by the battery:

  • Battery charge level directly affects system availability
  • High or continuous usage will reduce battery capacity
  • Regular charging via solar or camp site power is recommended

docs.title: Power Management Tips
docs.text:
To maximise battery life and system reliability:

  • Turn off unused lights and accessories
  • Monitor battery level daily
  • Use solar charging whenever possible
  • Avoid running high loads for extended periods

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• The 12V system is designed for low-voltage DC operation only.
  • Do not connect 240V appliances to 12V outlets.
  • Do not modify wiring or connections without authorisation.

⚠️ Improper use or modification of the 12V system may cause damage or unsafe operation.

Correct use of the 12V power system ensures reliable off-grid performance and long-term durability of your BreathTrailer.

docs.title: Inverter & City Power (240V System)
docs.text:
This section explains how 240V power is supplied in the BreathTrailer and how to correctly select between inverter power and camp site (City Power) electricity.

Correct use of the 240V system is essential to prevent overloads, system shutdowns, and equipment damage.

docs.title: 240V Power Overview
docs.text:
The BreathTrailer can supply 240V power using two different sources:

  • Battery Power (Inverter Mode)
  • Camp Site Power (City Power Mode)

Only one power source is active at a time, depending on the selector switch position.

docs.title: Power Source Selector Switch
docs.text: A power selector switch is installed at the front of the trailer, inside the trailer box.

docs.title: Switch Positions
docs.text:
Switch Position Power Source Battery Inverter (12V → 240V) City Power Camp site electricity

⚠️ Always confirm the switch position before using any 240V outlet.

docs.title: Inverter Mode (Battery Power)
docs.text: When the switch is set to Battery, 240V power is supplied by the inverter.

docs.title: How Inverter Mode Works
docs.text:
• Converts 12V battery power into 240V AC
  • Suitable for low to medium power appliances
  • Ideal for off-grid operation

docs.title: How to Use Inverter Mode
docs.text:
1. Ensure the battery system is ON.
  2. Set the power selector switch to Battery.
  3. Turn the inverter ON.
  4. Use the 240V outlets as required.

docs.title: Inverter Power Limitations
docs.text:
The inverter has a maximum power output.

⚠️ The following high-power appliances must not be used with the inverter: - Kettles - Heaters - Air fryers - Hair dryers

Using these appliances will overload the inverter and cause automatic shutdown.

docs.title: City Power Mode (Camp Site Power)
docs.text: When connected to camp site electricity, 240V power can be supplied directly to the trailer.

docs.title: How to Use City Power Mode
docs.text:
1. Connect the supplied 15A power lead to the camp site outlet.
  2. Plug the lead into the trailer box power inlet.
  3. Set the power selector switch to City Power.
  4. 240V outlets inside the trailer will be powered directly from the camp site.

docs.title: Solar Power System
docs.text:
This section explains how the solar power system operates in the BreathTrailer and how it contributes to battery charging during off-grid use.

The solar system is designed to work automatically and requires minimal user interaction.

docs.title: Solar System Overview
docs.text:
The BreathTrailer is equipped with a roof-mounted solar panel that charges the battery whenever sunlight is available.

Solar charging is managed automatically by the installed charging controller and does not require manual adjustment.

docs.title: Roof-Mounted Solar Panel
docs.text:
• Mounted on top of the trailer
  • Charges the battery continuously during daylight hours
  • Automatically starts and stops based on sunlight availability

☀️ Solar charging efficiency depends on weather conditions, sun angle, and panel cleanliness.

docs.title: Automatic Operation
docs.text:
• No switches or settings are required to enable solar charging
  • The system automatically prioritises safe and efficient battery charging
  • Solar charging can operate simultaneously with other charging sources

docs.title: Extra Solar Input (Solar Blanket)
docs.text: An Anderson plug is installed on the battery box to allow connection of an additional solar input.

docs.title: Using the Extra Solar Input
docs.text:
• Connect the supplied solar blanket to the Anderson plug
  • This increases total solar input and allows faster battery charging
  • Roof solar and solar blanket can operate together

✔️ Extra solar input is recommended when staying off-grid for extended periods.

docs.title: Solar Charging Tips
docs.text:
To maximise solar charging performance:

  • Park the trailer in direct sunlight when possible
  • Keep the solar panel clean and free of debris
  • Use the solar blanket to supplement roof solar when required
  • Monitor battery level regularly

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• Do not connect unapproved solar panels or power sources.
  • Ensure correct polarity when connecting external solar inputs.
  • Solar charging may be reduced in shaded areas or during poor weather.

⚠️ Incorrect solar connections may damage the charging system.

Proper use of the solar power system helps maintain battery charge and supports reliable off-grid operation of your BreathTrailer.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The BreathTrailer is equipped with an ANCEL BM300 Pro Smart Battery Monitor, providing real-time battery health monitoring, charging diagnostics, and historical performance data through a mobile application.

This system allows owners to actively monitor battery condition, helping prevent unexpected power loss during off-grid or campsite operation.

docs.title: System Capabilities
docs.text:
Real-Time Monitoring

The ANCEL BM300 Pro continuously monitors battery voltage and system health, providing live data directly to your smartphone.

  • Supports 6V / 12V / 24V battery systems
  • Measures battery voltage and charge status
  • Tracks charging and discharging behavior
  • Logs historical battery data automatically

docs.title: Mobile Application
docs.text:
Smart Battery App

The system connects via Bluetooth to the Smart Battery mobile application.

Application Features: - Available for iOS and Android - Free download - Supports monitoring multiple batteries - Automatic data synchronization - Alert notifications for abnormal conditions

docs.title: Diagnostic Functions
docs.text:
Advanced Diagnostics

The ANCEL BM300 Pro provides diagnostic insights beyond simple voltage readings.

  • Battery health analysis
  • Cranking system testing
  • Charging system verification
  • Historical test records storage

This helps identify weak batteries, charging issues, or system faults early.

docs.title: Electrical Safety & Protection
docs.text:
Built-In Protection

Designed for permanent installation and continuous operation.

  • Reverse polarity protection
  • Short-circuit protection
  • Ultra-low power consumption (~1mA average)
  • Safe for long-term connection

docs.title: Installation Notes
docs.text:
Installation Information

The battery monitor is pre-installed and permanently connected to the battery system.

  • No user configuration required
  • Operates automatically when the battery is connected
  • Designed for DIY users and professional service environments

docs.title: Supported Use Cases
docs.text:
• Off-grid camping
  • Long-term battery health tracking
  • Preventative maintenance
  • Electrical system diagnostics
  • Multi-trailer or multi-battery monitoring

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Why This Matters

The ANCEL BM300 Pro adds an extra layer of reliability and confidence to your BreathTrailer’s power system by giving you full visibility of battery performance at all times.

docs.title: Hot Water System – KickAss - For Breath Max read paper manual.
docs.text:
This section explains the operation and safe use of the KickAss 6L Portable Instant Gas Hot Water System installed in the BreathTrailer.

The system is designed to provide instant hot water for showering and general use while camping or off-grid.

docs.title: System Overview
docs.text:
The BreathTrailer is equipped with a KickAss 6L tank-less instant gas hot water system.

Key characteristics: - Instant hot water (no storage tank) - Automatic ignition - LCD temperature display - Australian gas safety certified - Portable and durable design

The system heats water only when it is flowing, providing hot water on demand.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Instant Hot Water Water is heated immediately as it passes through the unit.

  • Self-Igniting Operation The system automatically ignites when water flow is detected.

  • LCD Temperature Display Displays water temperature between 0°C and 45°C.

  • Gas Safe Certified Certified to meet Australian gas safety standards.

  • Durable Construction Powder-coated steel body designed for outdoor use.

  • Shower Head ON/OFF Switch Allows control of water flow to reduce water usage.

docs.title: Water Supply Options
docs.text:
The hot water system can be supplied with water using:

  • Mains water via hose connection
  • 12V pressure water pump connected to a water tank

⚠️ Important: The water pump must be turned ON for the hot water system to operate.

docs.title: Gas Requirements
docs.text:
• LPG gas cylinder is required (not supplied)
  • The system uses a new-style Australian-standard gas connection
  • Gas regulator and approved LPG hose are required

docs.title: Gas Connector Compatibility
docs.text:
Gas cylinders manufactured or tested after 01/04/2022 must use the new-style connector.

If an older gas bottle is used, it must be exchanged for a compatible cylinder at a swap-and-go centre.

docs.title: How to Use the Hot Water System
docs.text:
Follow these steps to operate the system:

  1. Ensure the water source is connected (mains water or water tank).
  2. Turn the 12V water pump ON.
  3. Connect the LPG gas cylinder and ensure the valve is open.
  4. Turn the hot water system ON.
  5. Open the shower head or tap.
  6. Adjust water flow and temperature as required.

Hot water will be supplied instantly when water is flowing.

docs.title: Safety Guidelines
docs.text:
• Never operate the hot water system without water flow.
  • Do not operate the system in enclosed or poorly ventilated spaces.
  • Always ensure gas connections are secure before use.
  • Turn off the gas supply when the system is not in use.
  • Allow the unit to cool before handling or storage.

⚠️ Improper use may result in gas hazards, burns, or equipment damage.

docs.title: Maintenance & Care
docs.text:
• Inspect gas hoses and connections regularly.
  • Keep the unit clean and free from dust or debris.
  • Drain water from the system when not in use or before storage.
  • Store the unit in a dry, well-ventilated area.

Correct operation of the hot water system ensures safe, reliable access to hot water during your BreathTrailer adventures.

docs.title: Water Tanks & Level Monitoring
docs.text:
This section explains the water tank configuration installed in the BreathTrailer, including fresh water storage, grey water collection, and level monitoring.

Proper understanding of the water tanks ensures reliable water supply and responsible waste management while camping.

docs.title: Water Tank Overview
docs.text:
The BreathTrailer is equipped with two water tanks mounted underneath the trailer:

  • Fresh Water Tank (Clean Water)
  • Grey Water Tank (Waste Water)

Each tank is designed for its specific purpose and must be used correctly.

docs.title: Fresh Water Tank
docs.text:
The fresh water tank stores clean water for:

  • Kitchen sink
  • Shower
  • General water use

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Dedicated drain valve
  • Level float sensor
  • Breather (overflow) valve

docs.title: Tank Breather (Overflow)
docs.text:
The fresh water tank includes a breather valve.

✔️ It is normal for water to drip or leak slightly from the breather once the tank is completely full. This indicates that the tank has reached maximum capacity and is functioning correctly.

docs.title: Grey Water Tank
docs.text:
The grey water tank collects used water from:

  • Kitchen sink
  • Shower
  • Other water outlets

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Dedicated drain valve
  • Level float sensor

⚠️ Grey water must be disposed of at approved dump points only.

docs.title: Water Level Monitoring
docs.text:
Both water tanks are fitted with level float sensors.

  • Water levels can be checked inside the kitchen area of the trailer
  • The display allows monitoring of both fresh and grey water levels

Monitoring tank levels helps prevent: - Running out of fresh water - Overfilling the grey water tank

docs.title: Draining the Water Tanks
docs.text: Both tanks can be drained when required.

docs.title: When to Drain
docs.text:
• After camping trips
  • Before long-term storage
  • When grey water tank is full
  • When winterising or cleaning the system

docs.title: Drain Valve Operation
docs.text:
• Locate the drain valves underneath the trailer
  • Open the appropriate valve to drain the tank
  • Ensure valves are fully closed after draining

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• Do not allow the fresh water tank to run completely dry when the pump is ON.
  • Do not overfill the grey water tank.
  • Always dispose of grey water responsibly.
  • Regularly check drain valves for leaks or damage.

Correct use and monitoring of the water tanks ensures reliable water supply, system longevity, and environmentally responsible operation of your BreathTrailer.

docs.title: Kitchen Sink – Hot & Cold Water
docs.text:
This section explains how to operate the kitchen sink in the BreathTrailer, including both cold and hot water supply.

The kitchen sink is supplied by the trailer’s water system and requires the water pump to be operating.

docs.title: Water Supply Overview
docs.text:
Water to the kitchen sink is supplied from the fresh water tank or mains water connection, depending on the system setup.

The sink can provide: - Cold water - Hot water (when the hot water system is in use)

docs.title: Cold Water Operation
docs.text:
To use cold water at the kitchen sink:

  1. Turn the 12V water pump ON.
  2. Open the kitchen tap.

Cold water will flow immediately when the tap is opened.

docs.title: Hot Water Operation
docs.text:
To use hot water at the kitchen sink, the following conditions must be met:

  1. Turn the 12V water pump ON.
  2. Ensure the hot water system is connected to LPG gas.
  3. Turn the hot water system ON.
  4. Open the kitchen tap.

Hot water will be supplied automatically once the system is operating.

docs.title: Water Pump Requirement
docs.text:
⚠️ Important: The water pump must be switched ON for both cold and hot water to operate at the kitchen sink.

If the pump is OFF, no water will flow from the tap.

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Turn the water pump OFF when the sink is not in use to save battery power.
  • Avoid running the water pump dry.
  • Monitor fresh water and grey water tank levels regularly.
  • Use hot water only when required to conserve gas and water.

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• Do not operate the water pump without water in the fresh water tank.
  • If water flow becomes inconsistent, check the pump and tank levels.
  • Ensure all connections are secure before use.

Correct operation of the kitchen sink system ensures reliable access to hot and cold water during your BreathTrailer trips.

docs.title: Fridge Operation
docs.text:
This section explains how to operate the 12V fridge installed in the BreathTrailer.

The fridge is designed for efficient off-grid operation and is powered directly from the trailer’s 12V battery system.

docs.title: Fridge Overview
docs.text:
The BreathTrailer is equipped with a 12V refrigerator, with capacity depending on the trailer model:

  • 30L
  • 60L

The fridge operates automatically once power is supplied and does not require connection to camp site electricity.

docs.title: Power Supply
docs.text:
• The fridge operates exclusively on 12V power
  • Power is supplied directly from the trailer battery
  • The fridge remains operational even when the trailer is not connected to camp site power

docs.title: How to Use the Fridge
docs.text:
To operate the fridge:

  1. Turn ON the main 12V power switch inside the trailer box.
  2. The fridge will start operating automatically.
  3. Adjust temperature settings on the fridge control panel if required.

✔️ No additional setup is required.

docs.title: Power Consumption
docs.text:
• Continuous fridge operation will draw power from the battery.
  • Battery charge level affects how long the fridge can run without recharging.

To maintain battery charge: - Use solar charging whenever possible. - Monitor battery level daily. - Avoid opening the fridge unnecessarily.

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Pre-cool food and drinks before placing them in the fridge.
  • Keep the fridge well ventilated.
  • Do not overload the fridge beyond its capacity.
  • Secure items inside the fridge during travel.

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• Ensure the fridge is switched OFF during long-term storage.
  • Do not use the fridge if the battery level is critically low.
  • If the fridge does not operate, check the main 12V power switch and battery charge.

Correct use of the fridge ensures efficient cooling and reliable performance during your BreathTrailer adventures.

docs.title: 🔥 Stove – Dometic PI8022 (2 Burner Hotplate)
docs.text:
Only for Breath Max

The Breath Max is equipped with the Dometic PI8022 two-burner hotplate, designed specifically for camper and caravan use. This compact and efficient cooktop delivers reliable cooking performance while maximizing bench space and safety.

docs.title: 🧩 Features
docs.text:
• Compact two-burner cooktop with improved cooking efficiency
  • Dual burners with strong and consistent heat output
  • Heat-resistant safety glass lid, protecting burners when not in use
  • Dual-purpose glass lid provides additional workspace when closed
  • Easy-to-clean detachable trivets
  • Stylish stainless-steel finish
  • Push-button Piezo ignition for easy operation
  • Duo-coloured control knobs for clear temperature adjustment

docs.title: 🔥 Cooking Performance
docs.text:
• Total heat output: 9.7 MJ/h
  • Left burner (Small): 3.8 MJ/h
  • Right burner (Large): 5.9 MJ/h

This configuration allows flexible cooking, from gentle simmering to higher-heat cooking.

docs.title: 📐 Specifications
docs.text:
• Model: Dometic PI8022
  • Number of burners: 2

docs.title: Power
docs.text:
• Burner 1 output: 1.1 kW
  • Burner 2 output: 1.8 kW

docs.title: Size & Weight
docs.text:
• Width: 480 mm
  • Depth: 370 mm
  • Height: 80 mm
  • Net weight: 3.58 kg

docs.title: ⚠️ Safety Instructions
docs.text:
Important Safety Information

  • Always ensure adequate ventilation when using the stove
  • Never leave the stove unattended while operating
  • Keep flammable materials away from the cooking surface
  • Turn off all burners and the gas supply when not in use
  • Allow the stove to cool completely before closing the lid or cleaning

docs.title: 🧼 Cleaning & Maintenance
docs.text:
Care & Maintenance

  • Clean the surface with a soft, damp cloth after use
  • Do not use abrasive or corrosive cleaners
  • Remove and clean trivets regularly
  • Periodically inspect burners and gas connections

docs.title: ❗ Important Notes
docs.text:
Gas Safety Notice

  • This appliance is designed for recreational and camping use only
  • Always follow applicable gas safety regulations
  • If a gas smell is detected, turn off the gas supply immediately and ventilate the area

docs.title: 🔥 Portable Gas Stove
docs.text:
Commonly used model: Coleman Triton 2 Burner Stove (Black)

The Portable Gas Stove is a convenient cooking solution designed for outdoor use, providing flexibility when cooking outside the trailer or at designated camping areas.

At Breath Trailer, we commonly use the Coleman Triton 2 Burner Stove, known for its reliability, portability, and ease of use during camping and outdoor activities.

docs.title: 🧩 General Features
docs.text:
• Portable two-burner gas stove for outdoor cooking
  • Stable and durable construction
  • Independent burner control
  • Suitable for camping, outdoor kitchens, and picnic areas
  • Designed to be used with external gas supply

docs.title: 🔌 Connecting the Gas Hose (Safe Connection Guide)
docs.text:
Gas Connection Safety

Improper gas connections can cause leaks, fire, or explosion. Always follow these instructions carefully.

docs.title: Step-by-step connection:
docs.text:
1. Ensure the gas supply is completely turned OFF
  2. Check the gas hose for:
  3. Cracks
  4. Cuts
  5. Signs of wear or damage
  6. Connect the hose firmly to the stove inlet
  7. Tighten the connection securely by hand or with an appropriate tool
  8. Do not overtighten
  9. Connect the other end of the hose to the gas regulator
  10. Ensure the regulator is correctly attached to the gas bottle
  11. Slowly turn ON the gas supply

docs.title: Leak test (mandatory):
docs.text:
• Apply soapy water to all connections
  • If bubbles appear:
  • Turn OFF the gas immediately
  • Re-tighten or replace the hose
  • Never use the stove if a gas leak is detected

docs.title: 🔥 Operating the Portable Gas Stove
docs.text:
Safe Usage Guidelines

Always operate the portable gas stove in a well-ventilated outdoor area.

  • Place the stove on a stable, flat, and non-flammable surface
  • Keep the stove away from walls, tents, and flammable materials
  • Never use the portable gas stove inside the trailer or enclosed spaces
  • Open the gas supply slowly before ignition
  • Ignite burners following the manufacturer’s instructions
  • Adjust flame using the control knobs as required
  • Always supervise the stove while in use

docs.title: ⚠️ Important Safety Rules
docs.text:
Critical Safety Information

  • Never use the portable gas stove indoors or inside the trailer
  • Never leave the stove unattended while operating
  • Keep children and pets away from the cooking area
  • Do not move the stove while it is hot or in use
  • Turn OFF the gas supply immediately after use
  • Allow the stove to cool completely before storage

docs.title: 🧼 Cleaning & Storage
docs.text:
• Allow the stove to cool completely before cleaning
  • Wipe surfaces with a soft, damp cloth
  • Do not use abrasive or corrosive cleaners
  • Remove food residues after each use
  • Store the stove in a dry, well-ventilated area
  • Disconnect the gas hose when not in use

docs.title: ❗ Important Notes
docs.text:
Usage Disclaimer

  • Portable gas stoves are intended for outdoor recreational use only
  • Always follow the stove manufacturer’s instructions
  • Always comply with local gas safety regulations
  • If a gas smell is detected: Turn OFF

docs.title: Awning – Kings 180° / 270°
docs.text:
This section explains how to safely set up, pack away, and care for the Kings 180° or 270° Awning installed on the BreathTrailer.

Correct use of the awning ensures safety, durability, and reliable performance in outdoor conditions.

docs.title: General Safety Information
docs.text:
⚠️ Always ensure the vehicle is stationary with the handbrake applied before setting up or packing away the awning.

⚠️ Do not deploy the awning in strong winds or extreme weather conditions.

Failure to follow these guidelines may result in equipment damage or personal injury.

docs.title: Awning Setup Instructions
docs.text:
Follow these steps to set up the awning:

  1. Ensure the trailer and tow vehicle are stationary and the handbrake is applied.
  2. Undo the zipper on the awning storage bag.
  3. Fold the top section of the awning bag over the mounting brackets.
  4. Allow the bottom section of the awning bag to hang freely.
  5. Undo all Velcro straps, starting from the rear of the awning.
  6. Gently roll the awning down, allowing it to hang.
  7. Attach the tension strap with carabiner to the cam buckle on the awning square pole.
  8. While holding the tension strap, walk in an arc around the rear of the trailer, allowing the awning to rotate into position.
  9. Once fully unfolded, hook the tension strap onto a suitable mounting point on the vehicle or trailer.
  10. Adjust the cam buckle to tension the canvas until it is tight and secure.

✔️ The awning is now fully set up.

docs.title: Awning Pack-Up Instructions
docs.text:
Before packing away, ensure the area around the awning is clear of obstacles and trip hazards.

  1. Loosen the tension strap and unhook it from the vehicle.
  2. Begin folding the awning back toward its stored position.
  3. Ensure the canvas is folded neatly while hanging.
  4. Once fully rotated into the closed position, roll the canvas upward starting from the bottom.
  5. Secure the rolled canvas using the hook-and-loop (Velcro) straps.
  6. Ensure the awning is secure and fully zip the awning storage bag closed.

docs.title: Weather Warnings
docs.text:
⚠️ If strong winds or extreme weather are approaching: - Pack away the awning immediately. - Use two people if necessary to safely control the awning.

⚠️ Avoid packing away the awning when wet. If the awning must be packed wet, open it again and allow it to fully dry as soon as possible.

docs.title: Care & Maintenance
docs.text:
To ensure long-term durability:

  • Clean the awning using cold water and a soft brush only
  • Do not use soap, detergents, petrol, oil, or solvents
  • Avoid creating sharp creases when packing the awning
  • Always allow the awning to dry completely before long-term storage
  • Regularly inspect pivot points, fasteners, and mounting brackets

Correct setup and care of the awning ensures safe use and long-lasting performance of your BreathTrailer outdoor equipment.

docs.title: Shower Tent – KickAss
docs.text:
This section explains the setup, use, and care of the KickAss Camping Shower Tent Awning installed on the BreathTrailer.

The shower tent provides a private area for showering, toilet use, or changing while camping or off-grid.

docs.title: Product Overview
docs.text:
The BreathTrailer is equipped with a KickAss vehicle-mounted shower tent, designed for quick deployment and durable outdoor use.

The shower tent can be used as: - Shower enclosure - Toilet/ensuite area - Changing room

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Ultra-fast setup (approximately 7 seconds)
  • Vehicle-mounted design using supplied brackets
  • Heavy-duty 300D rip-stop polyester fabric
  • UV-resistant material with internal lining
  • Prevents silhouettes and sagging
  • Compact external storage bag
  • Adjustable hanging straps (1.6 m – 2.1 m)
  • Lightweight design (approximately 7 kg)
  • Double-sided zip for easy access
  • Internal mesh storage pocket
  • Weighted curtain with structural bottom poles
  • Corrosion-resistant 6063 aluminium alloy frame

docs.title: Setup Instructions
docs.text:
Follow these steps to set up the shower tent:

  1. Ensure the trailer is stationary and the handbrake is applied.
  2. Unzip the shower tent storage bag.
  3. Fold the tent outward from the trailer.
  4. Allow the frame and fabric to drop into position.
  5. Secure the bottom of the tent using the supplied pegs if required.
  6. Adjust the hanging straps to suit ground level and trailer height.

✔️ The shower tent is now ready for use.

docs.title: Using the Shower Tent
docs.text:
The shower tent can be paired with: - A 12V water pump - The KickAss instant gas hot water system

This combination provides a complete off-grid shower solution.

⚠️ Ensure the water pump is ON and the hot water system is correctly connected before use.

docs.title: Pack-Up Instructions
docs.text:
To pack away the shower tent:

  1. Ensure the tent is clean and free from debris.
  2. Fold the tent neatly toward the trailer.
  3. Allow the frame to collapse into its stored position.
  4. Zip the storage bag fully closed.

⚠️ Avoid packing away the tent when wet. If packed wet, open and dry the tent as soon as possible to prevent mould or fabric damage.

docs.title: Care & Maintenance
docs.text:
To maintain the shower tent in good condition:

  • Clean with cold water and a soft brush only
  • Do not use detergents, solvents, or harsh chemicals
  • Allow the tent to dry completely before storage
  • Regularly inspect mounting brackets and fasteners
  • Store the tent securely in its storage bag when not in use

docs.title: Safety Notes
docs.text:
• Do not use the shower tent in strong winds or extreme weather.
  • Ensure the tent is properly secured before use.
  • Keep the area around the tent clear of trip hazards.

Correct use and maintenance of the shower tent ensures privacy, convenience, and reliable performance during your BreathTrailer camping experience.

docs.title: Double Door with Flyscreen
docs.text:
The BreathTrailer features a double door system with flyscreen, designed to improve ventilation, comfort, and insect protection while camping.

The flyscreen allows airflow into the trailer while keeping insects out, making it suitable for use in warm climates and off-grid environments.

docs.title: Intended Use
docs.text: The double door with flyscreen is intended to: - Improve airflow inside the trailer - Allow natural ventilation - Reduce insect entry when doors are open

docs.title: General Guidelines
docs.text:
• Ensure doors are fully secured before towing.
  • Do not force doors or flyscreen mechanisms.
  • Keep tracks and seals clean to ensure smooth operation.
  • Close and secure doors during adverse weather conditions.

docs.title: Maintenance Notes
docs.text:
• Regularly inspect door seals and hinges.
  • Keep flyscreen clean and free from debris.
  • Do not use sharp objects near the flyscreen material.

docs.title: Additional Information
docs.text: Further details, including operating instructions, care guidelines, and safety notes, will be added to this section in a future update of the manual.

docs.title: 15A Power Lead (Camp Site Power)
docs.text:
This section explains the use of the 15A power lead supplied with the BreathTrailer and how it enables connection to camp site (City Power) electricity.

Correct use of the 15A power lead allows safe battery charging and direct 240V power inside the trailer.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A 15A extension power lead is supplied with the BreathTrailer.

This power lead allows: - Charging the trailer battery when connected to camp site power - Supplying 240V power directly to the trailer outlets in City Power mode

docs.title: When to Use the 15A Power Lead
docs.text: Use the 15A power lead when: - Staying at powered camp sites - Charging the battery from mains electricity - Operating 240V appliances using City Power

docs.title: How to Connect Camp Site Power
docs.text:
Follow these steps to connect camp site electricity:

  1. Ensure all high-load appliances are turned OFF.
  2. Connect the 15A power lead to the camp site outlet.
  3. Plug the other end of the lead into the trailer box power inlet.
  4. Set the power selector switch to City Power.
  5. Confirm 240V power is available at the trailer outlets.

✔️ Battery charging will begin automatically via the installed battery charger.

docs.title: Safety Guidelines
docs.text:
• Always use the supplied 15A-rated power lead.
  • Do not use damaged or modified power leads.
  • Keep power leads away from water, heat, and sharp edges.
  • Disconnect camp site power before towing the trailer.
  • Do not overload camp site outlets.

⚠️ Using incorrect power leads or connections may cause electrical hazards.

docs.title: Storage & Care
docs.text:
• Coil the power lead neatly after use.
  • Store in a dry, clean location.
  • Inspect the lead regularly for damage or wear.

Proper use of the 15A power lead ensures safe and reliable operation of 240V systems in your BreathTrailer.

docs.title: Extra Solar Input (Solar Blanket)
docs.text:
This section explains how to use the extra solar input available on the BreathTrailer battery system.

The extra solar input allows faster and more efficient battery charging when additional solar power is required.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The BreathTrailer battery box is equipped with an Anderson plug that allows connection of an external solar input, such as a solar blanket.

This system is designed to work alongside the roof-mounted solar panel.

docs.title: Purpose of Extra Solar Input
docs.text: The extra solar input is intended to: - Increase total solar charging capacity - Reduce battery recharge time - Improve off-grid performance during extended stays - Compensate for limited sunlight conditions

docs.title: Compatible Solar Equipment
docs.text:
• Portable solar blankets supplied with the trailer
  • Approved solar panels with Anderson plug connection

⚠️ Only use compatible and approved solar equipment to avoid system damage.

docs.title: How to Use the Extra Solar Input
docs.text:
Follow these steps to connect an external solar source:

  1. Place the solar blanket or panel in direct sunlight.
  2. Ensure correct orientation for maximum sun exposure.
  3. Connect the solar blanket Anderson plug to the Anderson input on the battery box.
  4. Charging will begin automatically.

✔️ No additional settings or switches are required.

docs.title: Combined Solar Operation
docs.text:
• Roof solar and external solar input can operate at the same time.
  • The charging system automatically manages multiple solar sources.
  • Battery protection systems prevent overcharging.

docs.title: Solar Charging Tips
docs.text: To maximise performance: - Position the solar blanket to face direct sunlight - Adjust the panel position throughout the day if possible - Keep solar panels clean and free from debris - Avoid shading the solar blanket or roof panel

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• Ensure correct polarity when connecting external solar inputs.
  • Do not connect unapproved power sources.
  • Disconnect the solar blanket before towing the trailer.

⚠️ Incorrect connections may damage the charging system or battery.

Using the extra solar input improves charging efficiency and enhances off-grid capability of your BreathTrailer.

docs.title: Daily Operation Guide
docs.text:
This section provides practical guidance for the day-to-day operation of the BreathTrailer to ensure safe use, system efficiency, and long-term reliability.

Following these daily practices helps prevent issues and maximises off-grid performance.

docs.title: Daily Start-Up Checklist
docs.text:
Before using the trailer each day:

  • Check battery charge level
  • Ensure the 12V power system is ON
  • Confirm water pump is ON only when required
  • Verify gas connections if hot water will be used
  • Check fresh and grey water tank levels

docs.title: Power Management
docs.text:
To manage power efficiently:

  • Use 12V systems whenever possible
  • Turn the inverter ON only when 240V power is required
  • Switch the inverter OFF when not in use
  • Avoid running high-power appliances on battery power
  • Monitor battery levels throughout the day

docs.title: Solar Usage
docs.text:
• Park the trailer in direct sunlight when possible
  • Use the roof solar panel as the primary charging source
  • Connect the solar blanket if additional charging is required
  • Keep solar panels clean for maximum efficiency

docs.title: Water Usage
docs.text:
• Turn the water pump OFF when not in use
  • Monitor fresh water tank levels regularly
  • Avoid overfilling the grey water tank
  • Use hot water only when required to conserve gas and water

docs.title: Outdoor Equipment
docs.text:
• Set up awnings and shower tent only in suitable weather conditions
  • Always secure outdoor equipment properly
  • Pack away awnings and tents if weather conditions change

docs.title: End-of-Day Checklist
docs.text:
At the end of each day:

  • Turn off unused lights and electrical systems
  • Switch the inverter OFF
  • Turn the water pump OFF
  • Secure doors, awnings, and outdoor equipment
  • Check that the trailer is safe and secure for the night

docs.title: Travel Preparation
docs.text:
Before towing the trailer:

  • Disconnect camp site power
  • Disconnect external solar panels or blankets
  • Secure all loose items inside the trailer
  • Ensure doors and awnings are fully closed and secured

Consistent daily operation practices help ensure safe use, efficient system performance, and a trouble-free experience with your BreathTrailer.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:
This section outlines the basic maintenance requirements for the BreathTrailer to ensure safe operation, system reliability, and long-term durability.

Regular maintenance helps prevent faults, extends component life, and ensures the trailer remains in good working condition.

docs.title: General Maintenance Guidelines
docs.text:
• Perform regular visual inspections of all systems.
  • Address any faults or damage before using the trailer.
  • Use only approved replacement parts and accessories.
  • Maintenance should be carried out by a qualified or authorised technician when required.

docs.title: Coupling & Towing Components
docs.text:
Regularly inspect: - Trailer coupling for wear or damage - Safety chains and attachment points - Jockey wheel operation - Handbrake operation

Lubricate moving parts as recommended and replace worn components promptly.

docs.title: Electrical System Maintenance
docs.text:
• Inspect electrical cables, plugs, and connections for damage.
  • Check the condition of the 15A power lead.
  • Ensure battery terminals are clean and secure.
  • Monitor battery health and charging performance.

⚠️ Do not attempt electrical repairs unless qualified.

docs.title: Battery Maintenance
docs.text:
• Keep battery terminals clean and free from corrosion.
  • Ensure adequate ventilation around the battery box.
  • Avoid deep discharging the battery whenever possible.
  • Recharge the battery regularly using solar or camp site power.

docs.title: Gas System Maintenance
docs.text:
• Inspect LPG hoses and regulators for signs of wear or damage.
  • Ensure all gas connections are tight and leak-free.
  • Replace gas components according to manufacturer recommendations.

⚠️ Gas system servicing must be carried out by a licensed technician.

docs.title: Water System Maintenance
docs.text:
• Inspect water hoses and fittings for leaks.
  • Clean water tanks periodically to maintain water quality.
  • Drain water systems before long-term storage.
  • Check drain valves for correct operation.

docs.title: Awning & Outdoor Equipment
docs.text:
• Inspect awning fabric and stitching for wear.
  • Check mounting brackets and fasteners regularly.
  • Clean awnings and shower tents after use.
  • Ensure all outdoor equipment is completely dry before storage.

docs.title: Storage & Long-Term Care
docs.text:
If the trailer will not be used for an extended period:

  • Disconnect all power sources
  • Turn off the main 12V power switch
  • Drain water tanks and lines
  • Store power leads and accessories in a dry location
  • Protect the trailer from extreme weather if possible

Regular maintenance ensures safe operation and helps maintain the value and reliability of your BreathTrailer over time.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
This section provides guidance for identifying and resolving common issues that may occur during operation of the BreathTrailer.

If a problem cannot be resolved using the steps below, contact an authorised service provider.

docs.title: Possible Causes
docs.text:
• Main 12V power switch is OFF
  • Battery is discharged
  • Loose or disconnected battery connection

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
• Turn the main 12V power switch ON
  • Check battery charge level
  • Inspect battery connections and terminals

docs.title: Possible Causes
docs.text:
• Power selector switch in incorrect position
  • Inverter is OFF
  • Camp site power not connected
  • Faulty power lead

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
• Confirm selector switch position (Battery or City Power)
  • Turn inverter ON if using Battery mode
  • Check camp site power connection
  • Inspect the 15A power lead for damage

docs.title: Possible Causes
docs.text:
• Inverter overload
  • Battery voltage too low
  • High-power appliance connected

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
• Turn off connected appliances
  • Remove high-power appliances
  • Recharge battery using solar or camp site power

docs.title: Possible Causes
docs.text:
• Water pump switch is OFF
  • Fresh water tank is empty
  • Electrical connection issue

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
• Turn water pump ON
  • Check fresh water tank level
  • Inspect pump wiring and fuse

docs.title: Possible Causes
docs.text:
• Water pump is OFF
  • Gas cylinder is empty or disconnected
  • Hot water system is OFF

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
• Turn water pump ON
  • Check LPG gas supply and connections
  • Turn hot water system ON

docs.title: Possible Causes
docs.text:
• Main 12V power switch is OFF
  • Battery charge is low
  • Fridge settings incorrect

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
• Turn main 12V power switch ON
  • Recharge battery
  • Check fridge temperature settings

docs.title: Possible Causes
docs.text:
• Insufficient sunlight
  • Solar panel or blanket in shade
  • Dirty solar panel
  • Loose connection

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
• Move trailer or solar blanket into direct sunlight
  • Clean solar panel surface
  • Check solar connections

docs.title: Possible Causes
docs.text:
• Incorrect setup
  • Obstructions or wind conditions
  • Fabric packed away wet

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
• Recheck setup instructions
  • Pack away during strong winds
  • Dry fabric thoroughly before storage

docs.title: When to Seek Assistance
docs.text:
Contact a qualified technician if: - Electrical or gas faults persist - Damage to critical components is detected - Safety systems are compromised

Following these troubleshooting steps can resolve most common issues and help maintain safe, reliable operation of your BreathTrailer.

docs.text:

If you require help beyond the information provided in this manual, please use the contact details below.

docs.text:

Damage caused by: - Incorrect operation - Unauthorised modifications - Improper electrical or gas connections

may not be covered under warranty.

Refer to your warranty documentation for full terms and conditions.
